source.section: PDF page 60 Schedule CA (540) instructions, Line 5a and 5b (RRB-1099-R benefits in column A entered in column B) and Line 6; Form 540 lines 13 to 19 and 31 to 33 (PDF pages 39-40); PDF page 13 Line 18 standard deduction chart and Line 31; PDF page 75 Tax Rate Schedules; PDF page 39 Form 540 lines 7 and 9 ('X $153'); PDF page 12 Line 7 and Line 9; PDF page 14 Line 32 and the AGI Limitation Worksheet lines a to i

worked: Single, 67: railroad retirement benefits (RRB-1099-R, Tier 2) 30,000 taxable federally, interest 25,000, dividends 15,000; federal AGI = 70,000. Form 540 line 13 federal AGI = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age-65 addition = 52,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtractions: Schedule CA (540) line 5 column B, railroad retirement benefits (RRB-1099-R) included in column A, in full 30,000.00. Schedule CA Part I line 27 column B = 30,000.00 = Form 540 line 14. Additions (line 16): 0.00. Line 15 = line 17 California AGI = 70,000.00 - 30,000.00 = 40,000.00. Line 18 California standard deduction (single, PDF page 13 chart) 5,706.00. Line 19 taxable income = 40,000.00 - 5,706.00 = 34,294.00. Tax on 34,294.00 by the projection's brackets: 11,079.00 x 1% = 110.79; 15,185.00 x 2% = 303.70; 8,030.00 x 4% = 321.20; total 735.69. Line 31: the form uses the Tax Table for taxable income of 100,000 or less; the row 34,251-34,350 gives 736 (formula result kept in expected). Line 32 exemption credits: federal AGI 70,000.00 is not more than 252,203.00, so no AGI limitation; line 7 personal 1 x 153 = 153.00; line 9 senior 1 x 153 = 153.00; line 32 = 306.00. Line 33 = 735.69 - 306.00 = 429.69; no other credits (lines 34 to 47 nil), line 48 = 429.69. State income tax = 429.69.
accepted_approximations: Taxable income of 100,000 or less is taxed by the Tax Table (100-dollar rows, tax at the row midpoint); the projection uses the schedules' exact arithmetic.
